title: From smoke to symbiosis: dissecting KAI2 signaling in rice using the specific receptor agonist, dMGer
content: Forest fires release smoke-derived chemicals called karrikins (KARs) that trigger germination of “fire-following” plants, ensuring germination coincides with low competition and plentiful resources. Genetic analyses in Arabidopsis revealed an α/β-hydrolase receptor, KAI2 (D14L in rice), is required for KAR responses. KAI2 shares structural similarity with its paralog, D14, which perceives the plant hormone strigolactone (SL) and modulates aspects of plant development, such as shoot branching (Aquino et al 2020). Both KAI2 and D14 require the same F-box protein, MAX2 (D3 in rice), to target downstream regulators of the SMAX1-LIKE (SMXL) gene family for proteasomal turnover (Fig. 1a) (Nelson et al 2011; Conn and Nelson 2016).
